search_queries: gctx egress enable default in docs/guides/ai-context-delivery.md

first_useful_action.note: Located Default posture: identity-only (CE-1) and snippet opt-in rules.

answer: Flipping GCTX's identity-only default to snippets-on would invert CE-1: today every GCTX tool and graph:// resource defaults to identity-only (docs/architecture/graph-context-delivery-spec.md — Default posture: identity-only (CE-1)). Source-text egress requires (a) the named opt-in flag gctx.egress defaultVariant disabled (CE-9) and (b) a per-request client capability; with the opt-in unset the fallback is identity-only, not text (CE-12: no auto-enable on first use). Consent (CE-12) is an explicit operator action with a consequence statement that secret-scanned, path-filtered source text will be sent to the connected assistant/LLM provider — anvil gctx egress enable records that consent; disable reverts. Snippet path then runs CE-3 sensitive-path + gitignore filters and CE-2 deny-by-default secret scan fail-closed. Security.md repeats identity-only default and that once a snippet reaches a client, Anvil's local-first boundary does not extend into that provider. Making snippets the default would breach CE-1 Ready-gate posture and silent-default house rules; it would need an explicit product/privacy decision, not a quiet flip. Spec §11 trust boundary still keeps enforcement independent of any advisory synthesis.
